title: Philidor Defense: Hanham Variation
line: Black keeps its pawn on e5 with a knight behind it, and must watch the weak pawn by its king.

steps.text: The Philidor Defense: White attacks your pawn on e5 a second time.
Keep your pawn on e5: guard it with the knight from b8.

also.e5d4: Taking is the line of the lesson before. This lesson keeps the pawn.
also.g8f6: That is also played. This lesson guards with the other knight.

steps.after: This is the Hanham Variation. White's bishop aims at f7.

steps.text: A slip seen in a quarter of club games: the bishop to e7. The pawns trade, the queen threatens mate on f7, and its guard falls.
Back before the mistake. Stop the queen from coming to d5 first.
Move the pawn on c7 one square. It guards d5, so the queen cannot come there.

wrong.f8e7: That is the mistake you just saw: the pawns trade and the queen comes to d5.
wrong.g8f6: If the pawns trade on e5, the white knight jumps to g5 and hits f7 with the bishop, and Black cannot hold it.

also.e5d4: Taking the pawn is also sound. This lesson keeps the pawn on e5.

steps.text: Now the bishop can come to e7: the pawn on c6 keeps the queen off d5.
steps.after: White takes on e5; take back with the pawn. This is the main line: cramped, and engines give White a small edge.

summary: A knight behind the center pawn keeps it in place, but the weak pawn by the king needs care. Guard the key square first.
